name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Installs the toolchain named by `lean-toolchain`, resolves the dependencies, and hydrates
      # Mathlib from its own artifact cache. `build: false` stops the action there, so that build
      # artifacts can be restored before the build runs.
      - name: Toolchain and dependencies
        uses: leanprover/lean-action@38fbc41a8c28c4cbaec22d7f7de508ec2e7c0dd9
        with:
          auto-config: false
          build: false
          use-github-cache: false
          use-mathlib-cache: true

      # Build artifacts carry over between runs. Lake keys every artifact by a trace over its
      # module's source and the traces of its imports, so a restored olean is reused only when
      # everything it transitively depends on hashes identically. A change in a subject-specific
      # module therefore reuses cached artifacts for unchanged general mathematics.
      #
      # The key covers what changes elaboration from outside the source tree: the compiler, the
      # dependency revisions, and `lakefile.toml`, which carries `warningAsError` and the linter
      # set. The source tree is not in the key, since Lake's traces decide per module;
      # `restore-keys` is what allows a partial hit.
      #
      # Mathlib comes from its own artifact cache above rather than through here, since several
      # gigabytes through the Actions cache would cost more than it saves. CombinatorialGames is not
      # covered by that cache, so it is restored here. The project build also contains
      # selected-source artifacts under `.lake/build/highlighted` and exact InfoView states under
      # `.lake/build/proof-states`.
      - name: Restore build artifacts
        id: restore-build
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: |
            .lake/build
            .lake/packages/CombinatorialGames/.lake/build
          key: lake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lakefile.toml', 'lake-manifest.json') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            lake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lakefile.toml', 'lake-manifest.json') }}-

      # `lake build` is a gate in its own right. It elaborates every module under the authoritative
      # `ConwayRefinement.*` glob with `warningAsError = true`, which rejects `sorry`, runs
      # Mathlib's elaboration-time linters, and builds the audits below. The environment linters run
      # separately, below. Mathlib's line-length and whitespace rules live in its text-based
      # linter and are not part of that, which is why `style` is a separate audit.
      - name: Palomar Challenge drift audit
        run: scripts/check-palomar-challenge.sh

      - name: Build
        run: |
          echo "::group::Lake Build Output"
          lake build
          echo "::endgroup::"

      # Save as soon as compilation succeeds. A later audit or proof-guide failure must not throw
      # away a valid hour-long build; Lake's traces will reject stale artifacts on the next run.
      - name: Save build artifacts
        if: steps.restore-build.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: |
            .lake/build
            .lake/packages/CombinatorialGames/.lake/build
          key: lake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lakefile.toml', 'lake-manifest.json') }}-${{ github.sha }}

      # The Palomar comparator compiles the copied statement under a different module name.
      - name: Palomar comparator compatibility audit
        run: lake exe palomar-compatibility

      # Every declaration under ConwayRefinement reduces to propext, Classical.choice, and
      # Quot.sound. No sorry, direct or transitive, occurs there in a statement or a proof.
      - name: Axiom audit
        run: lake exe axioms

      - name: Module system audit
        run: lake exe module-system

      # Standalone statements either rest on Mathlib alone or additionally on CombinatorialGames.
      - name: Standalone Mathlib audit
        run: lake exe standalone-mathlib

      - name: Standalone CombinatorialGames audit
        run: lake exe standalone-combinatorial-games

      - name: Isolated-claim proof audit
        run: lake exe proof-links

      - name: Style audit
        run: lake exe style

      # Core documentation records current mathematics, without editorial labels or workflow
      # status that can silently become false.
      - name: Documentation audit
        run: lake exe documentation

      # General mathematics imports neither Hahn-series nor surreal modules; checks stay leaves.
      - name: Layering audit
        run: lake exe layering

      # Mathlib's default environment linters (simpNF, unusedArguments, ...) over every
      # declaration, from a driver generated from the source tree, parsed fail-closed against an
      # (empty) grandfathered baseline; `@[nolint]` uses must be allowlisted. See the script header.
      - name: Environment lint
        run: scripts/lint-env.sh

  proof-guide:
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The Mathlib cache and verified project artifacts expand to almost 9 GiB. Remove SDKs that
      # this job never uses before restoring them onto the GitHub-hosted runner.
      - name: Free disk space for Lean artifacts
        run: |
          df -h /
          sudo rm -rf -- /usr/local/lib/android /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc
          df -h /

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 11.19.0
          run_install: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: blueprint/src/web-reader/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install proof-guide reader dependencies
        working-directory: blueprint/src/web-reader
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install Tectonic 0.17.0
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          archive="$RUNNER_TEMP/tectonic.tar.gz"
          url="https://github.com/tectonic-typesetting/tectonic/releases/download/"
          url+="tectonic%400.17.0/tectonic-0.17.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
          checksum="8533d07f9ccbd7a65824b9e0459041bca34af1eb33daba48f59215593753a3b7"
          curl --fail --location --silent --show-error "$url" --output "$archive"
          echo "$checksum  $archive" | sha256sum --check --status
          tar --extract --gzip --file "$archive" --directory "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          sudo install -m 0755 "$RUNNER_TEMP/tectonic" /usr/local/bin/tectonic

      # The verified job has already compiled the checked commit and saved this exact key. The
      # fallback keeps pull requests useful when their token may restore but not save caches.
      - name: Toolchain and dependencies
        uses: leanprover/lean-action@38fbc41a8c28c4cbaec22d7f7de508ec2e7c0dd9
        with:
          auto-config: false
          build: false
          use-github-cache: false
          use-mathlib-cache: true

      - name: Restore verified build artifacts
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: |
            .lake/build
            .lake/packages/CombinatorialGames/.lake/build
          key: lake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lakefile.toml', 'lake-manifest.json') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            lake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lakefile.toml', 'lake-manifest.json') }}-

      # Exact proof states are cached per selected module by the extractor itself. This outer cache
      # carries those module entries between runners without coupling them to the immutable Lean
      # build cache saved by the verified job.
      - name: Restore proof-guide source cache
        id: restore-proof-guide-source
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: .lake/build/blueprint-source
          key: blueprint-source-v2-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          # The second prefix migrates the cache produced by the previous key format. Remove it
          # after the first successful v2 save.
          restore-keys: |
            blueprint-source-v2-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain') }}-
            blueprint-source-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lakefile.toml', 'lake-manifest.json') }}-

      # Generate the proof guide before the negative controls. Several blueprint probes mutate
      # generated files and verify that the checker rejects the resulting drift.
      - name: Build proof guide from the checked commit
        run: |
          source_revision=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          CONWAY_REFINEMENT_BLUEPRINT_SOURCE_REVISION="$source_revision" \
            CONWAY_REFINEMENT_BLUEPRINT_PUBLISHED=1 scripts/blueprint.sh build

      # Preserve a successful extraction even if a later publication check finds a problem.
      - name: Save proof-guide source cache
        if: steps.restore-proof-guide-source.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: .lake/build/blueprint-source
          key: blueprint-source-v2-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('lean-toolchain') }}-${{ github.sha }}

      # An audit that inspects nothing passes every commit. Each probe below is a defect the
      # corresponding audit must reject, and the failure must name that probe: an audit that fails
      # for an unrelated reason would otherwise look like a working one. These run last, after the
      # real audits have already passed on the unmodified tree.
      - name: Audits reject what they claim to reject
        run: scripts/audit-probes.sh

      - name: Check proof-guide publication
        run: |
          source_revision=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          CONWAY_REFINEMENT_BLUEPRINT_SOURCE_REVISION="$source_revision" \
            scripts/check-blueprint-publication.sh

      - name: Upload proof-guide PDF
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: proof-guide-${{ github.sha }}
          path: blueprint/blueprint.pdf
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload GitHub Pages artifact
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: blueprint/web

  deploy-guide:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: proof-guide
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy proof guide to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  attach-guide-to-release:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: proof-guide
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Download proof-guide PDF
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: proof-guide-${{ github.sha }}
          path: release-artifacts

      - name: Attach PDF to the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          pdf=release-artifacts/blueprint.pdf
          if gh release view "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "$pdf" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "$pdf" \
              --title "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --generate-notes
          fi

          node-version: "20"

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
